title: Man. Post. Cap. II §XVI: Garissoles Distinguitur / Placeus — consensus on action alone
pass_a_gloss: GAR. The imputation of sin is distinguished into Prior, or Antecedent, or Immediate; and Posterior, or Consequent, or Mediate. Not inconveniently indeed; nor do I doubt that if only a right explanation were applied, consent here could easily be established: if namely both imputations were referred to the same, that is, if it were understood of Adam's sin taken in the same signification, or of the action by which Adam first made himself guilty of injured Divine Majesty. PL. Why then is consent not established? Why am I opposed? For I referred both those imputations to the same, and understood them only of that action by which Adam first sinned. That is clearer than the midday sun, and I wonder it could be called into doubt. For that very distinction, to omit other things, makes this clear: for it cannot be taken of the imputation of habitual sin or corruption. For who would say that corruption is imputed before corruption, or after corruption; with corruption mediating, or without it mediating?
pass_b_english: Garissoles (§XVI): Sin's imputation is divided into prior—or antecedent, or immediate—and posterior—or consequent, or mediate. Not a bad division; and I do not doubt that if only it were explained rightly, agreement here could easily be reached—namely if both imputations were referred to the same thing, that is, to Adam's sin in the same sense, or to the act by which Adam first made himself guilty of offending the Divine Majesty. Placeus: Why then is agreement not reached? Why am I attacked? I did refer both imputations to the same thing, and understood them only of the act by which Adam first sinned. That is clearer than noon, and I wonder it could be doubted. The distinction itself, to say nothing else, makes this plain: it cannot be taken of imputing habitual sin or corruption. Who would say corruption is imputed before corruption, or after it—through corruption as means, or without it?
source_text:
GAR. Distinguitur imputatio peccati in Priorem, sive Antecedentem, aut Immediatam; & Posteriorem, sive Consequentem, aut Mediatam. Haud incommode sane; nec dubito, si modo recta explicatio adhiberetur, consensum hic facile stabiliri posse: si nempe utraque imputatio eodem referretur, id est, si intelligeretur de peccato Adami eadem significatione accepto, sive de actione, qua primum Adamus reum se fecit laesae Divinae Majestatis.

PL. Cur ergo consensus non stabilitur? Cur oppugnor? utramque enim illam imputationem eodem retuli, ac nonnisi de illa actione qua primum Adamus peccavit, intellexi. Id sole meridiano clarius est, & miror vocari potuisse in dubium. Illa enim ipsa distinctio, ut alia omittam, hoc clarum facit: non potest enim de peccati habitualis seu corruptionis imputatione accipi. Quis enim dicat corruptionem ante corruptionem, aut post corruptionem; mediante corruptione, aut ea non mediante imputari?
